levelName: Independent user, upper band of B1
summary: You talk about your QA work with ease. You describe your day, report a bug step by step and explain how your team has changed. When you need to persuade developers or explain testing to someone outside QA, you stop and search for words, and this is the main step to B2.

highlights.label: Your strongest area
highlights.note: You tell a work story in a clear order, one step after another.

highlights.label: Your main focus
highlights.note: Saying why a bug matters, to developers and to people outside QA.

highlights.label: Study next at
highlights.note: You are clearly above B1, so the next step is the language of B2: giving reasons, weighing options and holding your view.

atWork.note: This list comes from your interview, not from a real meeting, so use it as a guide.

criteria.name: Range
criteria.gloss: The words and phrases you can use
criteria.observed: You have the words for your own work: regression, exploratory testing, logs, priority, release. When the topic moves away from QA steps, you look for words, for example "how to say". For B2 you need phrases to explain impact and risk.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.observed: Your meaning is always clear, and your past forms are right. The -s for he, she and it is often missing: "the system create", "the user lose". For B2 this needs to become automatic.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.observed: On familiar QA topics you keep going without help. When you need to persuade or explain, you pause often to find words. For B2 you need a more even pace in these longer answers.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.gloss: How you take part in a conversation
criteria.observed: You answer every question directly and add useful detail. When the developers disagree in your example, the decision goes to the product owner. For B2 you need to keep your point and answer the other side.

criteria.name: Coherence
criteria.observed: Your bug story has a clear order, step by step. You link ideas with "because" and "so". For B2 you need more ways to connect a point with its reason and its result.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.observed: Your speech is clear and easy to follow. The stress in some longer words, for example "regression", is not in the usual place. For B2 the stress in your key work words needs to be natural.

evidence.title: A bug report in clear steps
evidence.quote: [[I reproduced it, I wrote the steps, I attached the logs and the video]], and I put it in Jira with high priority.
evidence.note: Each step follows the one before. A developer or a manager can follow it the first time.

evidence.title: Change over time, with numbers
evidence.quote: [[When I joined]], two years ago, we had almost everything manual. [[Now]] we have, uh, maybe seventy percent automated
evidence.note: You compare then and now and give a number. This makes the change easy to see.

evidence.title: An opinion with a reason
evidence.quote: I think it's better, [[because]] we find more interesting bugs.
evidence.note: You say what you think and why, in one sentence.

ceiling.text: Your A2 and B1 answers were confident. At B2 the interview got harder. When you had to make a case to developers and explain testing to a new product manager, you stopped and searched for words. Your answer about changing one thing in your team went better: you gave a clear reason.
ceiling.quote: So, um, [[I cannot explain in short]], sorry.

priorities.title: Make your case about a bug
priorities.said: Like, if the user lose money, it's not minor. But sometimes they, they don't agree and, uh, [[I don't know, the product owner decide]].
priorities.target: If [[a user loses]] money, [[it can't be]] minor. [[I understand your point, but]] the impact for the user [[is serious]].
priorities.why: At B2 you keep your view when people disagree, and you give the reason again in a new way.

priorities.title: Explain testing to someone outside QA
priorities.said: It is long because [[it is many cases]].
priorities.target: It [[takes]] long because [[there are]] many cases: [[different cards and different countries make many combinations, and]] every combination can have a bug.
priorities.why: Product managers and clients need the reason in one or two clear sentences, with an example.

priorities.title: Add -s after he, she, it and the system
priorities.said: when the user clicks twice fast, the system [[create]] two refunds
priorities.target: when the user clicks twice fast, the system [[creates]] two refunds
priorities.why: You already say "clicks". The same -s on every verb after one person or one thing makes your reports sound more exact.

recommendation.reason: You now join demos with UK clients and answer their questions. This course works on defect reports, release meetings, explaining risk to non-technical people and client demos.
recommendation.practiceTitle: Something to try before the course
recommendation.practice: Pick one bug from this week. Explain in two minutes, out loud, why it matters, as if to a new product manager. Use one example and the phrase "In short, …". Record it and listen for the -s after "the system" and "the user".
